# Pinned Unicode inputs for the S3 candidate

The four unmodified Unicode 17.0.0 UCD files are downloaded from the URLs in `sources.json`; that file records their SHA-256 digests. This matches `unicode-normalization` 0.1.25 (`UNICODE_VERSION = (17, 0, 0)`). The files are Unicode data, not source subject to the source-file line cap. The upstream copyright and terms remain in the files and `LICENSE.txt`.

`cargo test -p snapback4-core --test unicode_fold -- --nocapture` (from `snapback4/`) checks the digests, tests all five columns of every normalization row, includes every UnicodeData lowercase mapping and SpecialCasing code point, adds sigma/I/astral/scalar edge cases and every ASCII pair, and writes the native oracle to `target/unicode-fold.json`. Duplicate inputs are folded once after all normalization conformance assertions; their first source location is retained. The generated oracle records both the normalization crate's and Rust standard library's Unicode versions. Expected folds are NFC then Rust string lowercase, not Unicode case folding. Text-boundary refusals are generated by the native argument validator, so controls still exercise raw folding and also have their query refusal checked.

From `snapback4/`, with Node 24 on PATH, `node witness/idb.mjs unicode` builds the fixtures and shipped wasm and compares in the existing Chromium witness machinery. It prints every difference and the Age of every input/expected/actual code point, browser/V8 versions, whether ICU/Unicode versions were discoverable, and 7 measured page-apply samples after 2 warmups for each 4,000-row word-indexed fixture. Any difference exits nonzero; a missing browser/tool or failed launch is an error. Chromium does not normally expose its ICU/Unicode version through CDP: unknown is reported as unknown, never guessed from the Node process. `--node` runs the same wasm under Node as explicitly supplemental evidence; it does not replace Chromium. `--artifact /absolute/path/device.js` uses a retained measurement artifact (`device.wasm` beside it); `--timing-only` omits the differential for timing-only older artifacts that have no witness export. No command appends to metrics.

Pending author ruling: the candidate's `WebDevice.word_fold` export is a diagnostic witness hook, not an addition to the client contract. It calls exactly the helper used by `words::tokens`; measurements of the final candidate include its bytes. The native path and `Builtin::Lower` remain Rust implementations. No durable or wire format changes.
